# CANDIDATE: VOLATILITY_COMPRESSION_RIBBON_FADE

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the EMA ribbon (8,13,21,34,55) contracts to a tight band (<0.15% width), price often reverts to the ribbon mean; a fade trade opposite the short-term bias captures mean-reversion edge. This exists because low volatility periods create equilibrium conditions where extended moves away from the compressed ribbon are statistically likely to reverse.

## Mechanism

Entry: Calculate 8-EMA and 55-EMA distance as percentage of price. If distance < 0.15% (tight ribbon) AND the 5-minute bar closes opposite the ribbon slope (ribbon sloping up but bar closes below 21-EMA, or ribbon sloping down but bar closes above 21-EMA), enter fade trade (short if ribbon up, long if ribbon down). Exit: Stop at opposite side of ribbon band (chart-stop using 8-EMA or 55-EMA whichever is farther from price); target at ribbon midpoint or 1R, whichever is reached first. Regime filters: VIX < 20, time 11:30-13:30 ET, avoid first/last 30 minutes of session.

6. **Concentration:** Unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest to determine if top-5 days dominate P&L.
